Find the area $A$ between the curve $y=-{x}^{2}-8$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=2$ (shown above). Do not round the answer.

$A=$ 
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(-{x}^{2}-8)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-8{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{2}-8\cdot x{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-(\frac{(2)^{3}}{3}-0)-8(2-0) \\  & =-\frac{8}{3}-16 \\  & =-\frac{56}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is 

$$
A=-{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{56}{3}.
$$
